sentences.text: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii is an obligately anaerobic, non-motile bacterium of the human gut, regarded as one of the most abundant colonizers of the human colon.

Strains isolated from human faeces produce butyrate, formate and lactate as fermentation products and require acetate in the growth medium; the species was moved from Fusobacterium to the new genus Faecalibacterium.

A study of ulcerative colitis reported a reduction of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, described as a well-known butyrate-producing bacterium, in the faecal microbiota of patients compared with healthy individuals.
Work on inflammatory bowel disease describes its associated dysbiosis as characterised by a loss of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, whose supernatant exerts an anti-inflammatory effect.
A gnotobiotic study describes Faecalibacterium prausnitzii as a commensal that can be considered a sensor and a marker of human health.
